Launched in 1958, which British motorcycle — notable for being the smallest-engined model its manufacturer ever produced at just 250cc — bore a name evoking a royal anniversary celebration?
questions.explanation: The Norton Jubilee, introduced in 1958, was a lightweight twin-cylinder motorcycle with a 250cc engine — the smallest displacement Norton ever put into production. Its name referenced a celebratory milestone, fitting for a company with a long racing heritage. Despite its modest size, it represented Norton's attempt to compete in the growing commuter and lightweight bike market of the late 1950s.
